newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end lower despite gains by golds.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end lower despite gains by golds.

text.p: Toronto's key stock index ended lower on Friday, weighed down by a weak Canadian dollar and interest rate jitters.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index shed 29.48 points to close at 5835.31 in moderate turnover of 78.2 million shares worth C$1.04 billion ($740 million). Declining issues outpaced advances 492 to 405, with 310 issues flat.
Analysts said a weak dollar and interest rate fears took their toll on a market already weakened by Thursday's losses.

"We were set up for a negative day and then the Canadian dollar lost ground overnight and slowly through today, and that put upward pressure on our bills, so rising interest rates -- another bearish (indicator) for stocks," said technical analyst Katherine Beattie at MMS International.
"The only thing that really helped us was modest gains in golds, but that just wasn't enough to offset the negatives," she added.
Twelve of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes ended the day in negative territory, led by conglomerates, metals and banks.

Conglomerates shed more than 177 points or 2.44 percent to 7092.91, while metals dropped 44.89 points or 0.87 points to 5130.63. The financial services sector fell 46.12 points or 0.77 percent to 5972.17.
The gold group led the gainers, rising 35.82 points or 0.41 percent to 8781.95.

The market was expected to remain volatile ahead of U.S. economic data due out next week. U.S. employment cost, gross domestic product and payroll employment data are seen as a key indication of whether U.S. interest rates will rise further.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd. led active issues, closing down 0.35 at 3.25 in heavy trade. The troubled Calgary, Alberta exploration firm said it expected to receive an interim report by the end of next week on the Busang audit being conducted by Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd.

Shares in BC Sugar Refinery Ltd. ended up 2.35 at 14.96 in turnover of more than 1.2 million shares after Balaclava Enterprises Ltd. said on Thursday it intended to offer to buy 7.85 million common shares of the sugar company at C$15 ($10.73) each.
Placer Dome Inc. shares were up 0.30 at 22.25 as more than one million shares. The gold miner said on Thursday it would sell its Endako molybdenum mine in British Columbia.
